text:
Kris Letang is 39, has played 1,255 games, all for Pittsburgh, and won three Stanley Cups. The question this week isn't how he's playing; it's whether he finishes his career in Pittsburgh. The New York Times asked where Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin and Letang go from here with the Penguins' season spiraling, and RMNB wrote that the team is preparing for a possible fire sale with hard decisions looming for its legends.

The hockey itself has been better than the moment. He has nine points in 20 games, six in his last 10, and Pittsburgh holds 56.5% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, more than five points better than when he sits. His shot still has heat (85th percentile in top speed by NHL Edge). The weak spot is finishing: one goal on 35 shots, and our wins-added measure has him near the bottom of the league because the shots haven't gone in at big moments. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 93rd percentile of defensemen for primary shot assists last season. Evolving-Hockey's 2025-26 numbers had him around replacement level.
